text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- When Pope John Paul II arrives for two-day visit to the Bosnian capital, the presidency's Serb member, Momcilo Krajisnik, will not be present at the airport because of security reasons. But he will be present at the national museum when the Pope meets Bosnian leaders the next day.
- Bosnian presidency decides that the country's white flag with lillies will be used as an official flag for the Papal visit but there will be no official anthem or honour guard.
- Presidency agrees on a basic outline for a central bank and asks the bank's steering board to prepare laws for the next presidency session.
- Mayor of divided town of Mostar, Ivan Prskalo, a Croat, describes the current situation in the town as better then ever.

- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation president, Vladimir Soljic, meets U.S. Generals Carl Vaughan and Crosby Saint to discuss possible consequences of proposed withdrawal of American troops from Bosnia in 1998.

- Due to an outstanding debt, a Russian gas company which supplies Bosnia with natural gas shuts down valves and not a single cubic centimeter of gas is flowing to the country now, local gas company says.

- Moslem-Croat federation's prime minister, Edhem Bicakcic, and Bosnian Moslems religious leader reis-ul-ulema Efendy Mustafa Ceric condemn attacks on religious buildings in Bosnia and call on authorities to be more efficient in finding perpetrators.

- Moslem chairman of presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, formed a "council of president Izetbegovic" which already convened once. Its job will be to advise the president in resolving complicated issues. The council consists of ten prominent Bosnians including co-prime minister Haris Silajdzic, diplomatic sources say.
- NATO-led Stabilisation Forces offers its help in providing security for visit of Pope John Paul II to Sarajevo this weekend.

- Director of the World Bank's mission in Bosnia, Rory O'Sullivan, expresses concern that Bosnia has not yet fulfiled programme of International Monetary Fund and thus delayed holding of international donors conference for reconstruction. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
